reason: Restore original fighter cabin after style reference leaked freighter cabin; correct aft baydoor arrow and side wing projection.

variants.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit the three-view sheet in IMAGE 1. Preserve its newly designed hull, ROUND aft drum with its existing recesses, neck shape, repair panels, colors, wings, SINGLE rear engine, typography and page layout. Make only the technical corrections below.

1. REPLACE THE WRONG CABIN IN ALL THREE VIEWS.
The current cabin in image 1 accidentally came from a FREIGHTER. Its divided little rectangular blue windows below the windshield, large opaque lower face, yellow frame all around its roof, and box-shaped brown chin with a square device are WRONG for this fighter.
IMAGE 2 is the ACTUAL ORIGINAL FIGHTER CABIN and is the exact required replacement. IMAGE 3 shows the same actual cabin fitted to the original fighter. IMAGE 4 also shows it. Transplant that cabin faithfully into the design of image 1 in place of its wrong cabin. Keep the same original fighter scale, tall down-hanging placement at the front of the neck and recognizable entire module.
Specific fighter cabin features from image 2:
- A large sloping muted-blue FRONT WINDSHIELD. Just below the thin original horizontal yellow/black divider there is ANOTHER BROAD CONTINUOUS BLUE FRONT BAND, almost the full width of the front, with clipped lower corners. There are NO thick upright posts cutting that band into little freight-truck windows.
- Tall side glass panes and broad original weathered gray side framing.
- A small projecting plain weathered-metal BROW, NOT a decorative yellow rim all around the canopy top.
- Below the broad blue band is an opaque stepped gray CHIN shell, a dark-red rectangular side inset, small blue corner slots and the separate lower yellow/black BUMPER stripe.
- The very bottom is a SHORT TAPERED POLYGONAL POINT, as in image 2. REMOVE the freighter's hanging brown rectangular box and square fixture.
Do not invent new glazing, armour, horns, a bubble canopy or a face. Copy the original fighter module with its correct proportions; do not redesign it. Preserve the illustrated material style while faithfully reproducing geometry. This cabin correction is the most important change.

2. FIX THE BAYDOOR ARROW / FREE TRAVEL.
The current arrow wrongly points toward the nose. In TOP the nose is UP and the engine is DOWN. The arrow must point DOWN toward the rear engine, label BAYDOOR. Image 4 shows actual native closed/open behavior: the dorsal rectangular lid slides AFT and slightly UP into a pocket beneath the raised shoulder, not forward or rotating. Keep the hatch closed and its rectangular outline. Show a plausible small recessed receiving slot under the rear shoulder where necessary; no fixed block sitting across the lid's moving plane. Do not redesign the hull or the aft circle for this.

3. CONSISTENT FLIGHT WINGS.
Retain the existing FORWARD-SWEPT wing shape in TOP: nose UP, roots lower on page than outer leading tips. SIDE nose RIGHT: the wing must project DOWN-RIGHT from root, toward the cockpit, not down-left toward the rear. Keep flight anhedral down/out and short blunt/clip-tipped wings, no folded-up outer panels, no pointed blades.
Keep clear articulation at inner carrier and outer wing; do not add exterior rods or frames. New medium detail, repair style and all drum geometry stay unchanged. No new objects, no extra views, no additional explanatory text.

Output ONE revised three-view sheet with same R01/R02 title. All three views must show the SAME original fighter cabin. No freighter reference is provided here because its cabin must not be used.
R01: preserve the offset round inset and deep crescent pocket. The current SIDE wing points down-left: explicitly redraw that wing down-right to agree with TOP. Do not change the correct forward TOP wing sweep.
